contact_edits.before: Twin performances that make the Mamet pauses sing come from Peter Donaldson as the most abrasive member of the sales force, nursing grudges from way back, and William Webster, jowly and pouchy, as the most pathetic, facing the same defeat as Levene but without the same fight in him. Jordan Pettle gets the manager absolutely right, savouring his power and, beneath his collegiate veneer, as ruthless and venal a barracuda as the boys out in the field. Ken MacDonald's sets do well by the restaurant, less well by the office; the two are symbolically linked when the wall menu of one turns into the contest-scoreboard of the other. I'm not convinced that a play at once so full and so spare needs this kind of illustration, but I guess it serves for a play in which dog voraciously eats dog after first sharing a table with him. - Glengarry Glen Ross runs until May 9. Call 416-866-8666 for tickets.
